label: sec:mobius-energy-intro
html:
The previous section produced the universal R-matrix for \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)), fixing the braiding on \mathbf{Rep}(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))). With the braiding in hand, we extract a numerical invariant of a closed strand: an energy that grows when the strand folds back on itself. We define this categorically and verify that it reproduces the classical Möbius energy in the limit q \to 1.

Proposition: Categorical recovery of Möbius energy anchors this section. It writes the energy of a knot embedding \varrho \colon S^1 \to \tau(A) as a Frobenius double integral built from the Hopf comultiplication and the q-Hodge star, then identifies its q \to 1 limit with the classical Möbius energy up to a topological constant. Lemma: Classical limit of the Frobenius--Hopf kernel is the repulsive 1/r^2 tracks the kernel through the limit, showing that the Frobenius pairing degenerates onto the \mathrm{SU}(2) Killing form. Corollary: Obstruction to self-intersection details the consequence: at q \neq 1, non-cocommutativity of the Hopf structure makes the energy diverge whenever two non-adjacent strands approach within the fibre \tau(A). Lemma: q-deformed commutator replaces 1/r^2 with a hard kernel at r = \hbar_q records the substrate-side picture: the divergence has a finite cutoff at the Planck scale \hbar_q. The next section, Crossing energy and Coulomb charge, converts this self-avoidance kernel into an energy contribution localised at each crossing.
